newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean gold market seen quiet ahead of holiday.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean gold market seen quiet ahead of holiday.

text.p: South Korea's gold market was unusually quiet ahead of the Lunar New Year holiday with demand dampened by recent labour unrest and the Hanbo Group loan scandal, dealers in Seoul said on Tuesday.

Hanbo Steel Co, flagship of the Hanbo Group, the 14th largest conglomerate in South Korea, piled up about five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans from banks and financial institutions before it became insolvent on January 23.
"Usually there is good (gold) demand before the Lunar New Year," a bullion dealer said.
"But this year demand has disappeared. No one expects demand to pick up under the current domestic economic conditions."
The dealers said most local retail sellers of gold are expected to close shop from January 6 until January 11 for the Lunar New Year holiday.
Since January, South Korea has been battered by the financial troubles of the Hanbo Group, which came as another blow to an economy already struggling with a slump in exports.
South Korean domestic gold prices have fallen in line with weak international prices, but the decline has been partially offset by the won's sharp fall against the dollar, dealers said.

Gold producer LG Metals' daily selling price for the precious metal, which is regarded as a benchmark for the local bullion wholesale market, has fallen by 70 won per gram to 10,050 won from 10,120 won a week ago.
LG's silver price also fell by two won a gram to 152 won from 154 won a week earlier.
The won has plummetted in line with the Japanese yen's weakness against the dollar on world markets and South Korea's snowballing trade deficit.
South Korea posted a record monthly trade deficit of $3.48 billion for January, compared with $2.13 billion a year earlier.
The won fell to an 84-month low of 867.00 won to the dollar during Monday's mid-morning trading as the country's trade deficit heightened dollar demand, dealers said.
The customer telegraphic transfer selling rate, posted by the Korea Exchange Bank, rose to 870.20 won against the dollar from 858.40 a week ago.
The rate is regarded as a benchmark for local foreign exchange rates for companies.
